Coverage (layers, regions): Historical presence and designation layers. Buildings lists: 130 'Warisan Kebangsaan' (National Heritage, declared 2007-2018) and 125 'Warisan' (Heritage, gazetted 1977-2020). Separate lists for archaeological sites and other categories.
How systematic: Structured but as PDF tables per category: number, site, gazette number or declaration date and place. No coordinates, no descriptions.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): PDF download and table extraction. No searchable database found.
Historical versions: Yes: gazette and declaration dates per entry.
Framing notes: Chinese-community sites look rare: one found in the 130 National Heritage buildings (Leong San Tong Khoo Kongsi, Penang, 2018) and none identified in the 125 Heritage buildings. Read by automated summary; recheck by hand.

Owner type: Host state agency (World Heritage site manager)
Coverage (layers, regions): Historical presence in the George Town World Heritage site: more than 5,000 buildings; 82 Category I buildings, gateways, cemeteries and sites; Category II mostly shophouses.
How systematic: Building inventory exists (Special Area Plan) but no list, database or map is published on the page.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Manual. Ask GTWHI for the inventory or use the Special Area Plan document.
Framing notes: Lists 'Chinese temples' and 'water villages (clan jetties)' among building types, alongside mosques, churches and Hindu temples: multicultural framing.

Coverage (layers, regions): Chinese cemetery with over 12,000 graves, some claimed to date to the Ming dynasty (per Wikipedia). A 1980s development proposal made it a national controversy; in 2005 it was reported it would be gazetted as an ancient monument.
How systematic: No register entry found online; evidence is news and community sources.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Manual. Current legal status still to confirm.
Historical versions: Yes: 1980s dispute and 2005 gazettal report give dated framings.
Framing notes: Good test case: community, state and (later) Chinese-embassy narratives attach to the same hill.

Source: Kazakhstan State List of Monuments of History and Culture of Republican Significance
Coverage (layers, regions): Designation layer for Kazakhstan, including Silk Roads components in Zhetysu.
How systematic: List published as a legal act; also regional lists of local significance.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Not yet read: the legal portal refused automated access. Test in Phase 2 (adilet.zan.kz).

Source: Kyrgyzstan State List of monuments of republican significance
Coverage (layers, regions): Designation layer: 583 objects on the State List out of about 2,000 immovable monuments (2015 heritage concept).
How systematic: Legal text grouped by type (history, archaeology, architecture, art, combined).
Historical versions: Yes: list and amendments are dated.
Framing notes: Silk Roads components carry dual names, modern and historical: «Ак-Бешим (Суяб)», «Бурана (Баласагын)», «Красноречинское (Невакет)». No China reference in the naming.

Coverage (layers, regions): Over 45,000 archaeological sites across Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Xinjiang (China); about 250,000 digitised archive files.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Open-access core without registration; sensitive data on request. Rights: all rights reserved, so reuse needs permission.
Framing notes: Treats Xinjiang as part of a Central Asian landscape; partner logos include Northwest University (China).

Coverage (layers, regions): Institutional engagement at Angkor: dated news by temple and by international team (India, US, Japan, South Korea, France, China).
How systematic: Semi-structured dated news posts. No project database.
Historical versions: Yes: posts dated from at least 2024.
Framing notes: China appears as one partner among many: 'China-Cambodia Government Team for Safeguarding Angkor'. Technical, not civilisational, wording.

How systematic: No online register or list found in this pass.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Not found. Needs Chinese-language search and literature in a later pass.

Source: National Museums of Kenya: gazetted sites and monuments
Coverage (layers, regions): Designation layer: 208 gazetted sites and monuments in the Wikipedia compilation, with gazette dates and coordinates. Coast entries include Gedi (1970), Mambrui (1935), Manda (1956), Siyu (1958), Pate (1982), Shanga (1983), Fort Jesus (1970).
How systematic: Official source is Kenya Gazette notices (kenyalaw.org); Wikipedia offers a structured table.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Wikipedia table or Wikidata for structure; gazette notices for verification.
Framing notes: NMK's 2024 announcement of Gedi's World Heritage listing calls it 'a testament to the Swahili culture' and does not mention China.

Source: National Register of Historic Places (National Park Service)
Coverage (layers, regions): Designation layer for the US: all listed properties, National Historic Landmarks, removed and eligible properties.
How systematic: Highly structured: Excel spreadsheets (updated 2026-05-22) and a GIS geodatabase.
Historical versions: Yes: listing dates; nomination forms on NPGallery.
Framing notes: Ethnic association is coded under 'Area of Significance' (e.g. 'Ethnic Heritage: Asian') but applied inconsistently, so Chinese-related places are undercounted. About 10% of places are identified with a cultural or ethnic community.

Source: NPS Asian American and Pacific Islander theme study, Appendix II study list (2017)
Coverage (layers, regions): About 90 properties that may be eligible for National Historic Landmark status, grouped by community; roughly 35-40 Chinese American (approximate). Examples: Bok Kai Temple, Weaverville Joss House, China Alley, Rock Springs Massacre Site.
How systematic: PDF table: property, location, National Register listing year, criteria.
Framing notes: Frames sites as part of American national history.

Source: Chinese Railroad Workers in North America Project (Stanford)
Coverage (layers, regions): Railway-worker sites and archaeology of overseas Chinese communities.
How systematic: No downloadable site list or database on the page; publications and an archaeology network.

Source: Victorian Heritage Database (Heritage Council of Victoria)
Coverage (layers, regions): Designation and narrative layers for Victoria: 454 places match the keyword 'chinese' (includes false positives), each with coordinates, summary and statement of significance.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Open JSON API (tested 2026-10-05): id, name, latlon, summary, authority, register number.
Historical versions: Heritage studies carry author and year.
Framing notes: Bendigo Joss House: 'sole reminder' of a once extensive Chinese gold-rush community. Local-history framing.

Coverage (layers, regions): More than 20,000 natural, historic and Indigenous places across national lists.
How systematic: Structured; files and APIs listed on data.gov.au.

Source: Chinese Australian Historical Society select list; CHIA image database
Coverage (layers, regions): Community-compiled select list of Chinese Australian heritage sites by state (temples, market gardens, cemeteries, Broome Chinatown), linking to official registers. CHIA: archived catalogue of historical images.
How systematic: Semi-structured web list; CHIA is archived.
Framing notes: Community advocacy for listing: shows who is asking for recognition.

Coverage (layers, regions): Crosswalk and thin site coverage: 93 Chinatowns (82 with coordinates, 74 with a Chinese label); 2,028 Chinese temples of which about 207 are tagged outside mainland China, Taiwan, Hong Kong and Macao (including historical states); 16 in Malaysia. 6,184 items carry a UNESCO World Heritage ID.
Framing notes: No framing text. Use as an ID and name crosswalk, not as the site list.
Reliability: Medium; very incomplete for diaspora sites.

Coverage (layers, regions): Much denser than Wikidata: 938 Taoist, Chinese-folk or Confucian places of worship in Malaysia, 392 with a Chinese name.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Overpass API. Public servers timed out on multi-country queries; query one country at a time or use a regional extract.
Framing notes: No framing text. Best seed list for temples; needs checking against registers.

Source: AidData Global Chinese Development Finance dataset v3.0
Coverage (layers, regions): Institutional engagement layer: 20,985 Chinese-financed projects in 165 countries, 2000-2021. Includes heritage aid, e.g. RMB 90 million grant for the Angkor Royal Palace restoration (2018, project 62500).
How systematic: Highly structured; ZIP download plus GeoJSON locations.
Access method (preliminary, for Phase 2): Bulk download; keyword filter for heritage, restoration, archaeology.
Framing notes: Neutral descriptive records with funder and implementer.

Coverage (layers, regions): More than 1,000 Chinese temples in Singapore with founding years, addresses, deities, inscriptions and links to mother temples in China. Outside the candidate regions; a model for the data to collect.
Framing notes: Records ties to 'mother temples' in China: a ready-made diaspora-to-China link field.
